title: Nebraska Franchise Practices Act: cumulative location and sales criteria
description: Work through the separate tests that can govern an ongoing franchise relationship, even after a sales notice is filed.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Apply the state definition and every criterion
paragraphs: The Act has its own definition, including specific nonalcoholic-beverage wording, petroleum exclusion, franchise fee and good-cause concepts. A SAMP notice or federal franchise result does not decide this relationship question.
Section 87-403 requires all three criteria below; these are not general minimum sizes for entering Nebraska.

rows: The defined fixed place displaying/selling goods or offering/selling the franchisor’s services. Office, warehouse, storage place, residence and vehicle are expressly excluded.
Covered product/service gross sales exceeding $35,000 during the 12 months immediately before the lawsuit is filed.
More than 20% of the franchisee’s gross sales intended to be or derived from the franchise.

sections.heading: Coverage is not a promise of indefinite renewal
paragraphs: Section 87-404 generally combines good cause with written reasons at least 60 days in advance, with an abandonment branch and specified immediate-notice grounds. Noncompetition provisions have their own scope.

Section 87-404(1) also preserves a contract making the franchise nonrenewable or renewable only on stated reasonable conditions. Apply the actual contract, action and branch rather than treating 60 days as automatic permission or renewal as guaranteed.

practicalOutput: Test the exact premises and both sales criteria before relying on ongoing protections or choosing an exit procedure.
limitations: Actual definition, cumulative criteria, contract terms and exceptions require application. This is not complete Nebraska sales or operating-law coverage.
learningSummary: A Nebraska office and high expected branded income do not alone establish Franchise Practices Act protection. Its place-of-business and two sales tests must all be met.
seoTitle: Nebraska Franchise Practices Act: Location and Sales Tests

title: Nebraska nonexempt SAMP earnings claims: arithmetic versus purchaser evidence
description: Learn why a possible sales calculation is different from evidence supporting an income claim to a prospective buyer.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Establish the actual sales-law route
paragraphs: Section 59-1729 applies to covered seller-assisted marketing-plan earning-potential representations. Read it with the franchise exemption and other exclusions; this is not a finding that every marketing restriction survives for every qualifying exempt franchise. Federal financial-performance requirements remain separate.

sections.heading: A correct $4,000 calculation is not attainment evidence
paragraphs: The fictional calculation is 20 cleaning accounts × $200 monthly profit per account = $4,000 per month if the assumptions hold. It does not show purchasers obtained or retained those accounts or earned that profit.

The statute says multiplying sales by profit per sale is insufficient substantiation. Required information includes the seller’s selling history, number and percentage of purchasers forming the representation’s basis, and purchasers known to attain the stated results.
Identify the actual group, period and cost definition rather than converting selected inputs into a claim. An “illustrative” label does not supply missing support.

sections.heading: Keeping support is different from providing it
paragraphs: The rule addresses prescribed supporting data and disclosure to the purchaser. Apply the required step for leaving that data with the purchaser; an internal sales file alone may not satisfy it.
Nonexempt SAMP advertising also has applicable seller-identification requirements. Review the actual income message across slides, scripts, emails and calculators, not just one written version.

practicalOutput: Before using the figure with a purchaser, establish the applicable route, actual attainment support and prescribed delivery—not just the arithmetic.
limitations: This is the stated nonexempt SAMP branch. No future buyer result or universal exempt-franchise claims rule is established.
learningSummary: For Nebraska’s stated nonexempt SAMP earnings rule, multiplying accounts by assumed profit is not enough support for a purchaser-facing claim. The seller needs the prescribed actual-experience information and purchaser disclosure.
seoTitle: Nebraska Nonexempt SAMP Earnings-Claim Evidence

title: New Hampshire equipment dealer scope: sales and service rights
description: Understand why an industrial-equipment or authorised-service partner may need a dealer-law review even without a car showroom.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Identify the equipment and granted rights
paragraphs: RSA 357-C includes specified farm, utility, forestry, industrial, construction, yard and garden equipment. Its definitions also require particular sellers, rights and arrangements; the equipment list alone does not establish coverage.

Separate equipment sales, distribution, authorized service and warranty rights, including actual supplier and parts dependence. The specified single-line dealer exception and express treatment of service-only fleet, government or rental-vehicle arrangements need their own conditions.

sections.heading: This note does not supply an exit deadline
paragraphs: Covered relationships have good-faith, good-cause, notice and protest provisions. The actual RSA 357-C:7 route must be examined for the intended event. A contract saying “good faith” does not establish compliance, and this page supplies no universal notice period or compensation entitlement.

practicalOutput: Identify the added products and service/warranty rights before applying a dealer definition or choosing an exit process.
limitations: Limited to the named scope inquiry. Actual exceptions and the event-specific RSA 357-C:7 procedure remain unresolved.
learningSummary: New Hampshire’s dealer chapter can include specified industrial and other equipment, not just passenger cars. Adding machine sales or authorized service rights to a labour-only business can change which definitions need examination.
seoTitle: New Hampshire equipment dealer scope: sales and service rights

title: Alacrity payroll judgment: admitted misclassification, overtime and record violations
description: The historical judgment records admitted payroll violations. For a cleaning owner, the practical question is who resolves hours and pay when two businesses share the work.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: What the court record establishes
paragraphs: The identified consent judgment concerns Alacrity Employment Services and Hawaii Care and Cleaning, District of Hawaii case 1:24-cv-00567. The judge dated it 14 January 2025; it was filed the next day. Paragraph I.Q expressly admits willful misclassification, overtime and time/payroll-record violations during the stated 2021–2024 period. This was an agreed judgment, not a contested trial or a no-admission settlement.

It orders $1.9 million in back wages, $1.9 million in liquidated damages and $50,000 in civil penalties: $3.85 million in total. It also addresses reclassification, accurate records, payroll practices, nonretaliation and supervisor training. Those ordered amounts are not proof of collection or distribution.

sections.heading: Who resolves a disputed hours entry?
paragraphs: The order involved a labour-supplying operation and a cleaning company. In your arrangement, the useful questions are who assigns buildings, changes schedules, sets pay, records hours and can correct an entry. The contract and actual instructions need to agree.

Consider a separate fictional visit: a building-access record suggests a longer visit than payroll shows, but the supervisor points to a signed timesheet. The signature does not explain the discrepancy. The supervisor and payroll reviewer must establish what work occurred and keep the reason for any correction; the worker also needs a route to raise the problem.

Travel between jobs, breaks and pay calculations need the rules applicable to that work. Neither the court’s result nor an access log alone determines the outcome for another staffing or franchise arrangement.

practicalOutput: Check who can correct hours and pay when the supplier, supervisor and worker disagree.
limitations: Historical identified judgment only; no complete current docket or recovery finding. An apparent installment/date inconsistency remains unresolved, so no payment schedule is stated.
label: Real case — allegations, admissions and historical procedural scope are distinguished
learningSummary: Using a labour supplier does not answer who checks the hours or corrects payroll. The Alacrity judgment connects the companies’ operating arrangements with admitted violations and obligations to change their practices.
seoTitle: Alacrity cleaning payroll consent judgment and admitted violations

title: Will the restaurant’s menu work in the premises you want to lease?
description: A smaller outlet may look cheaper until its food process, storage or equipment fails to fit. Check the proposed operation before relying on the site saving.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The menu can change the site decision
paragraphs: A takeaway counter, full kitchen, mobile unit and commissary—a separate supporting kitchen—can need different answers. If a central kitchen supplies the outlet, identify what preparation remains on site, how deliveries work and what storage and equipment are needed.

A compact unit is not a proven saving if that process requires a different layout or equipment. Compare the revised operation with another site before spending more. A supplier’s machine specification or landlord’s consent does not establish the relevant authority’s acceptance.

sections.heading: Use the rules for the actual address
paragraphs: FDA’s 2026 Food Code is a model for regulators, not an edition that automatically governs every restaurant. The state, county, city, tribal or territorial authority may use another adopted edition or its own requirements.

Give the actual food and building/use authorities the address, operator, menu, process and equipment. Resolve the questions that could change the lease, design or purchase: plan review, water/wastewater, inspections and staff training where applicable. An opening date in a business plan is not an authority-confirmed date.
The restaurant’s operating permissions are also separate from the rules for offering franchise rights to a prospective partner.

practicalOutput: Resolve whether the proposed menu and preparation process fit the address before committing further to the lease or equipment.
limitations: No address-specific food, building, equipment or inspection approval, fee or opening period is established.
learningSummary: Before committing to a restaurant site, establish where food will be prepared, stored, heated, cooled and served. Landlord consent, food-authority acceptance and building/use permission answer different questions.
seoTitle: Restaurant premises: menu, central kitchen and local permission

title: Online fitness memberships: can the studio stop the next charge?
description: When the brand sells memberships but the studio controls payments, a cancellation request must reach the person who can stop the charges.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The order at checkout matters
paragraphs: For an Internet transaction with a negative-option feature—charges continuing until the customer takes action—15 U.S.C. §8403 requires material terms before billing information is obtained, express informed consent before charging, and simple mechanisms to stop recurring charges.
A terms page delivered after checkout does not establish the first requirement. Card details alone do not establish the required consent.

sections.heading: Follow the request into the payment account
paragraphs: In the fictional brand/studio setup, the brand receives a stop-charge request but the local studio’s payment system never receives it. The customer can keep being billed even though both contracts mention cancellation.

Test the actual path from the terms screen through consent and payment, then a request to stop further charges. Decide who receives it, who can act in the payment account and who tells the member what happened. A platform compliance badge does not demonstrate that this particular configuration works.

Freezes, transfers, refunds and complaints also need an accountable business. Pricing classes and staffing is a separate commercial question; collecting membership cash does not establish the cost of delivering the service.

practicalOutput: Send a test stop-charge request through the real brand-to-studio process and establish who prevents the next recurring charge.
limitations: This covers the cited Internet negative-option statute. State health-club, renewal, refund and cancellation rules remain separate; the test does not certify all-law compliance.
learningSummary: A member sees one service even if the website, studio and payment account belong to different businesses. A cancellation clause is little use when the request stops at the brand inbox.
seoTitle: Online gym memberships: consent and stopping recurring charges

title: Clinical testing: are you collecting specimens or running a laboratory?
description: Before choosing equipment or a partner, establish where each human test happens. Collection, laboratory testing and payment involve different decisions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Where will the test actually happen?
paragraphs: A proposed site might only collect specimens for another laboratory, perform testing itself or do both. A referral arrangement can add another business. Identify which role your proposed site has, where specimens are tested, who orders the tests and how results reach the customer.
This matters when choosing a partner. A general branch manager may be able to organise premises and sales but cannot replace the laboratory’s required professional roles.

sections.heading: What CLIA establishes
paragraphs: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services says the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) regulate human laboratory testing for health assessment or for diagnosis, prevention or treatment of disease. Requirements vary with test-method complexity.

“Waived” is a testing category, not a general release from certificates or operating duties. The actual method, category and any applicable exception must support the chosen certificate pathway. A foreign credential or brand agreement does not establish U.S. permission.

sections.heading: Before spending on the laboratory
paragraphs: Have the proposed laboratory operator identify the actual test methods, location, laboratory director, personnel and quality arrangements needed for that pathway. A pending application is different from issued permission.
State laboratory and professional-practice requirements are separate. So is payer enrollment: permission to perform a test does not establish which insurer will reimburse it or on what terms.

practicalOutput: Establish the test methods and performing laboratory before ordering equipment or hiring for a presumed certificate category.
limitations: This is a federal CLIA starting point, not a certificate, clinical, state-professional or reimbursement determination.
learningSummary: A small test menu does not establish an exemption. The test’s purpose, method and performing laboratory determine which CLIA questions to resolve before you commit to equipment or staff.
seoTitle: CLIA: specimen collection versus running a testing laboratory

title: Home-care payroll: does nonenforcement justify a cheaper wage budget?
description: The Labor Department’s enforcement instruction does not change the underlying requirements. It cannot, by itself, establish the payroll saving in your prices.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The regulation and bulletin do different jobs
paragraphs: Current 29 CFR 552.109 says third-party employers may not claim the companionship minimum-wage/overtime exemption or the live-in overtime exemption described there.

The Department of Labor’s 25 July 2025 Field Assistance Bulletin, FAB 2025-4, separately directs Wage and Hour Division staff not to apply the 2013 provisions while that policy remains applicable. The bulletin expressly does not alter statutory or regulatory requirements or create enforceable rights.

A proposed rule is not an effective repeal. An older public answer should not silently displace the later bulletin. Final-rule developments, litigation, private claims and state/local law still need current assessment for the actual arrangement.

sections.heading: Price the work you actually plan to supply
paragraphs: Separate companionship, personal care, trained nursing and other healthcare tasks. Establish who recruits, employs, directs, schedules, records time and pays, including travel between clients and longer visits.

Until the applicable treatment is resolved, make the wage assumption explicit rather than choosing the cheapest interpretation as fact. A two-client day can change hours and cost when travel or visits run longer; this article supplies neither an exemption decision nor an invented wage rate.
Federal payroll treatment does not establish state home-care licensing or permission to perform nursing tasks. Those decisions affect which service the agency can sell in the first place.

practicalOutput: Resolve the actual employment treatment before relying on an overtime saving in hiring or customer prices.
limitations: The bulletin is neither repeal nor immunity. Individual exemption/status, private enforcement, state/local law and service/professional permissions are not determined here.
learningSummary: A home-care agency cannot treat an agency’s nonenforcement policy as a confirmed exemption. The actual employer, duties and applicable law still determine the payroll treatment it can rely on.
seoTitle: Home-care overtime: regulation versus FAB 2025-4 enforcement policy

title: Lead-renovation work: check firm certification before advertising
description: Covered renovation can bring duties before the first job is won. The business’s certification and an individual worker’s training are different requirements.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Which property and work are you selling?
paragraphs: The cited Renovation, Repair and Painting (RRP) guidance concerns paid renovation disturbing paint in relevant pre-1978 housing and child-occupied facilities. Building age and use, actual paint information, surfaces, work and affected area matter, together with the defined exceptions.

Repainting and window replacement in one quotation are still different tasks. Window replacement, demolition and prohibited practices need particular attention under the exception rules. New-looking paint or describing the job as minor does not establish a lead-free or minor-work exception.

sections.heading: Check the business as well as the worker
paragraphs: Permission to use the brand does not supply the undertaking firm’s certification, and a worker’s training does not substitute for that firm record. Identify the firm, people performing/supervising work and any subcontractor.

Covered delivery may involve training, pre-renovation education and work practices as well as customer communication and waste arrangements. Include those applicable costs before copying a home-market whole-house price.
State-authorised lead programmes and state/local contractor or trade requirements need separate attention. The federal RRP starting point is not a complete contractor licence.

practicalOutput: Screen the actual property and tasks, then establish the firm and individual requirements before covered advertising or work.
limitations: No job-specific exception, lead-safety method or contractor authorisation is established.
learningSummary: A renovation brand should screen older-property work before selling it. EPA says firms cannot advertise covered renovation without firm certification; waiting until a signed job can be too late.
seoTitle: EPA RRP firm certification before renovation advertising

title: HVAC work: which technician can service this equipment?
description: Start with the actual refrigerant and task. Brand training and a name on a staff list do not establish the technician’s authority or availability.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: What the cited federal overview covers
paragraphs: EPA’s Section 608 overview identifies certification for technicians maintaining, servicing, repairing or disposing of equipment that could release ozone-depleting refrigerants. The actual category and any exception must fit the equipment and work.

That overview is not a complete account of every substitute refrigerant. The person’s certification and limits need to be established before covered work is assigned; an overseas manager or brand diagnostic course is not automatically a qualified substitute.

sections.heading: A qualified technician must also be available
paragraphs: If the specialist also covers a distant area, a corridor-wide response guarantee may fail even though the credential is correct. Test actual dispatch, travel and backup rather than treating the staff roster as proof of cover.

State trade licensing, local project permissions, recovery equipment and disposal remain separate questions. Price the actual specialists, parts, tools and support needed for the promise; the fuller capacity discussion is linked below.

practicalOutput: Identify the exact equipment and task before assigning a technician or promising a response across the area.
limitations: Limited federal overview only: no complete refrigerant regime, technician category, state trade or permit determination.
learningSummary: Before assigning HVAC work, identify the equipment, refrigerant, release-related task and intended technician. This limited EPA overview cannot supply a certificate answer for an unspecified system.
seoTitle: EPA Section 608 certification scope for proposed HVAC work

title: Buying or moving a California salon: what happens to the licence?
description: The fitted premises and old licence are not the same purchase. Check the owner/location record and each practitioner’s authority before adding services.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Match the licence to the actual change
paragraphs: The Board of Barbering and Cosmetology describes a new application and prior closure record for its specified ownership changes, and a new application after moving. Establish which change is taking place rather than treating the old establishment licence as transferable.

Then check the people delivering the services. The establishment record does not establish each practitioner’s authority. A doctor’s supervision does not expand a beauty licence into medical work, and the brand’s course certificate does not decide that scope.

sections.heading: A new treatment also changes the exposure question
paragraphs: For a smoothing treatment, the permitted service and the employer’s chemical duties are different checks. OSHA says products containing or releasing formaldehyde can trigger formaldehyde and hazard-communication requirements, including relevant assessment, protection and training.

The actual formulation and heating/mixing process, frequency, ventilation, room arrangement, safety data sheets and worker roles matter. Historic tests or a formaldehyde-free label do not establish current exposure, and changing bottles is not automatically a complete safety solution.
Local premises/sanitation and any product import or distribution responsibilities also remain separate from the California beauty-licensing record.

practicalOutput: Resolve the owner/location application and actual practitioner scope before relying on the old salon’s licence or selling an added service.
limitations: California licensing example and federal exposure starting point only; no actual product, exposure, local-site or all-state service approval.
learningSummary: A California salon licence is tied to its actual owner and location. Buying the equipment or taking over the lease does not establish the new operator’s permission or every worker’s service scope.
seoTitle: California salon ownership changes, moves and service scope

title: California auto repair: get the customer’s authority before extra work
description: The service desk and technician need to know what the customer agreed to. Business registration, specialist inspection roles and waste responsibilities are separate.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Before the technician does more
paragraphs: BAR’s January 2026 Write It Right guide describes estimates and recorded customer authority before covered repairs or extras, with linked transaction records. The desk needs to know what was agreed before the technician undertakes that work.

The guide has specific preventive-maintenance conditions and commercial-agreement/roadside boundaries. Calling every job maintenance does not establish the same treatment. Use the actual job and applicable conditions before choosing an exception or form.

sections.heading: Ordinary mechanics and specialist inspections differ
paragraphs: BAR says a general automotive repair mechanic does not need an individual BAR licence. That does not settle the repair business’s requirements or Smog and safety-inspection station/technician roles. Match the actual operator and services to those records; brand training is not a substitute.

sections.heading: Know where the resulting materials go
paragraphs: EPA’s used-oil guidance distinguishes generator, collection, transport and processing roles under 40 CFR Part 279, including good-condition, nonleaking container expectations. State rules can be stricter. Paying a collector does not establish that the workshop met all its own duties.

Oil, solvents, antifreeze, filters and batteries need separate identification: use, contamination, mixtures and disposition can change the analysis. The premises’ bays, drainage, containers, collection access and relevant fire/building/spill questions also need actual site answers.

practicalOutput: Trace one covered job from estimate to customer approval and any extra-work approval before changing the service desk’s process.
limitations: California defined repair/licensing and federal used-oil scope only; no complete repair form, actual exception, inspection, waste classification, site or cleanup approval.
learningSummary: A covered repair should not run ahead of the customer’s recorded authority. First identify the service, the business and any specialist role, then follow the estimate and approval through to the actual work.
seoTitle: California auto repair estimates, extra-work authority and business roles

title: Import packaged food or use a U.S. co-packer: compare the whole job
description: A manufacturing quote can look cheaper because label, quality or import work is missing. Identify the work before treating the price difference as a saving.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: What does each quote include?
paragraphs: For importing finished products, identify the actual producer, facilities, importer, label, shipment quantities and timing. For a U.S. co-packer—a business making or packing for the brand—identify the facility, recipe tolerances, packaging and division of quality work.

If one quote includes a label or quality task and the other leaves it unassigned, the difference is a scope gap, not yet a saving. Minimum orders, lead time and stock funding also change the cash required. A missing tariff or compliance cost is an unknown, not zero.

sections.heading: Registration is not approval of the food
paragraphs: FDA’s startup guidance describes registration for covered manufacturing, processing, packing and holding facilities, with specified exemptions. FDA/USDA allocation, product rules and retail/state-local requirements depend on the commodity and actual activity.
A restaurant exemption cannot simply be borrowed for a separate wholesale facility using the same brand. Facility registration also does not approve the food or label.

The actual ingredients, process, package and customer channel determine the product-specific questions. Assign label, preventive controls, records, quality and importer-program work between the brand, processor and importer, including who responds when the formulation or supplier changes.

practicalOutput: Compare complete supplier scopes and stock-funding needs before selecting the apparently cheaper production route.
limitations: No product, registration exemption, importer-program or comprehensive food-safety decision is made for an actual product.
learningSummary: An overseas producer, a U.S. co-packer and the brand can divide the same product’s work differently. The lower quote is not comparable until the omitted responsibilities and stock costs are understood.
seoTitle: Import packaged food versus U.S. co-packer responsibilities

title: Federal alcohol registration is not the restaurant’s selling licence
description: TTB registration, local retail selling authority and an import or wholesale role are different. Establish the actual seller and address before relying on alcohol revenue.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: What the federal retailer guidance covers
paragraphs: TTB describes federal dealer registration before the covered retail business begins, per-location treatment and receipt records. Its retailer guidance concerns sales for consumption both on and off the premises.
Identify the actual retail entity and locations/channels. Federal dealer registration is not a state/local selling licence, import permit or product approval.

sections.heading: What could change the opening plan?
paragraphs: Establish the actual state/local category, site suitability, ownership and application or transfer process before counting on alcohol sales. Buying the assets does not establish automatic licence transfer, and a landlord or supplier’s consent is not government selling authority.

If the overseas brand also owns or supplies the product, separate who imports, produces or wholesales from who sells to consumers. A home-country distribution right does not establish those U.S. permissions.

A forecast without alcohol can show dependence on wine revenue, but it does not establish permission to open the restaurant or an interim licence. Food, building and other opening requirements still apply.

practicalOutput: Establish the actual seller and site’s selling route before using alcohol revenue to justify the lease or launch.
limitations: Federal retailer starting point only; no state/local licence, product/import approval, transfer outcome or universal processing period is supplied.
learningSummary: A federal retailer registration does not establish permission to sell alcohol at the proposed premises. The restaurant’s seller, state/local licence and any separate supply role need their own answers.
seoTitle: Federal alcohol retailer registration versus state liquor licence

title: Puerto Rico: can you take a customer back from your partner?
description: A reserved exit clause may not settle a Puerto Rico dealer change. Understand the actual relationship before reallocating accounts, terminating or not renewing.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Does Law 75 cover the relationship?
paragraphs: The reviewed Spanish consolidation includes real responsibility for distributing goods or providing services by concession or franchise in the Puerto Rico market. What the partner actually does matters more than the agreement’s label. Not every franchise, distributor or service partner is automatically a protected dealer.
Consider who develops customers, holds stock, hires people, provides service and invests locally. Those facts help establish the relationship to which the proposed change would apply.

sections.heading: What changes when you reclaim an account?
paragraphs: Article 2 addresses termination, impairment and nonrenewal without just cause, even where the contract reserves unilateral exit. Article 2A contains specific impairment presumptions and qualifications. These provisions do not make every change unlawful, but an expiry date alone does not settle the question.

Fictional example: an industrial-maintenance partner develops customers and employs technicians. After two years the brand wants its largest account back. Before reallocating it, establish who won and supported the customer, the reserved-account terms, investment, performance concerns and the exact proposed change. This example establishes neither protected status nor damages.
Review the agreement and proposed notice against that history, including any opportunity to correct performance. Statutory damages factors are not an automatic refund or a reliable damages forecast.

practicalOutput: Assess the proposed account or exit change against the actual dealer relationship before sending a notice.
limitations: Based on the Spanish government consolidation revised 13 November 2020; the English explanation is not an official translation. Later amendments and controlling cases remain unchecked.
Forum/arbitration wording must be assessed with applicable federal law; this does not invalidate every outside-Puerto-Rico arbitration clause.

Federal franchise duties apply to territorial franchises subject to exemptions. Independent sales, company and staffing questions remain separate; Puerto Rico’s inside-customs-boundary status does not settle product duties or territorial taxes.
learningSummary: Before reclaiming a Puerto Rico account, consider what your local partner has built and undertaken to do. Law 75 can make that a dealer-relationship question even if the contract reserves an exit or direct-sales right.
seoTitle: Puerto Rico Law 75: taking accounts back or ending a dealer deal

title: U.S. Virgin Islands: what your operator needs from DLCA
description: Check the local operator’s DLCA licensing, initial or renewal tax instructions, and any credentials needed for technical work.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: What DLCA checks
paragraphs: Use the local business’s legal name and any trading name, and identify its site on St. Thomas, St. Croix or St. John. Your brand agreement gives private brand rights; it does not complete the public licensing process.

DLCA’s instructions identify the following checks. The fire, health and professional requirements depend on the activity and location; this is not a requirement to visit every agency in one fixed order. Some checks are handled electronically on the applicant’s behalf.
bullets: Entity or trading-name registration and the appropriate business-licence category.
Initial tax clearance and police review.
Zoning and applicable fire or health review.
Applicable professional-board and personnel requirements for regulated work.

sections.heading: Is this a first application or a renewal?
paragraphs: DLCA lists tax clearance for an initial application. Its renewal instruction says a licence is issued without confirmation of tax clearance, while the business remains responsible for current tax obligations and possible later action. A renewal therefore does not establish that unpaid tax has disappeared.
Check the current filing destination: some links on the reviewed DLCA page are old.

sections.heading: Adding HVAC changes the question
paragraphs: Fictional example: a facilities partner plans cleaning and air-conditioning maintenance. DLCA lists mechanical/HVAC professions among its board-certification categories, so the actual technician tasks and applicable credentials need checking. Brand training does not establish a government qualification.
Describe the mechanical work before promising it to customers. Check the proposed site’s applicable reviews too, without assuming that every cleaning business needs a health inspection.

practicalOutput: Ask DLCA which licence category and site or professional reviews apply to the named operator’s proposed services.
limitations: DLCA operating licensing only; no approval of this business or its work is established.
The federal Franchise Rule includes territorial franchises subject to exemptions; independent territorial dealer/franchise law remains unresolved here.
USVI is outside the cited U.S. customs territory. Equipment and product shipments need their own route-specific review.
learningSummary: For a first USVI business-licence application, DLCA lists tax clearance, police review and zoning, plus fire, health or professional reviews where applicable. Renewal has different tax-clearance instructions.
seoTitle: USVI business licence: DLCA, tax clearance and regulated work

title: Guam: does the partner’s licence cover your company’s work?
description: Identify which company conducts Guam business and whether its actual services fall under general or separate trade licensing.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: When the foreign company needs authority
paragraphs: The cited provision requires a covered foreign corporation to obtain both a business licence and a certificate of authority before transacting business in Guam. Its listed exclusions matter: owning a subsidiary alone does not automatically mean the parent conducts the subsidiary’s business. The actual entity form and activities must be assessed.

sections.heading: Which services does the licence cover?
paragraphs: Chapter 76 describes an annual licence for covered non-professional service activity. It excludes services an employee provides to the employer, while section 76103 addresses services licensed under other provisions. Cleaning equipment, electrical repairs and engineering advice should therefore not be assumed to share one general-service route.
Describe the tasks to identify the relevant licence or profession. The Business License and Permit Center directory helps locate the office; it does not make every listed permit applicable.

sections.heading: Before promising the commissioning date
paragraphs: Fictional example: a Singapore brand trains a Guam partner and sends a manager to commission equipment. The partner hires technicians, stores parts and repairs systems. Check the parent’s own Guam activity, the operator’s service categories and any regulated work the visitor performs. Company authority does not establish professional credentials or the individual’s permission to work.

practicalOutput: Resolve the parent’s activity, the operator’s service categories and the visiting technician’s work permission before promising delivery.
limitations: Federal territorial franchise scope is subject to exemptions; independent Guam sales, relationship and tax requirements are not cleared here.
Guam is outside the cited U.S. customs territory. Product, origin, importer, actual route and quarantine questions need their own answer; no shipment charges or staffing approvals are established.
learningSummary: The Guam operator’s licence does not answer what your overseas parent or visiting technician may do. Start with each actor’s actual work, contracts and location.
seoTitle: Guam company authority and service-business licensing

title: CNMI: will a new service or island office need another licence?
description: CNMI’s rule ties general business licences to business lines and locations. Check a new site, rental activity or asset purchase before relying on an existing licence.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: What an expansion changes

These are different starting events; 360 days is not a general invitation to wait.

The summary permits received foreign currency to pay or offset eligible overseas expense obligations without first bringing it back. Its footnote excludes foreign securities investment and purposes requiring prior BOT permission, including foreign FX/baht trades, related baht derivatives and gold payments without import. It is not unrestricted netting.

For American support receipts used to pay a trainer, identify the full fee, withholding, separate expense and actual dates, then establish whether the proposed use fits. BOT’s current-hosted bank guideline lets banks ask for further documents or information where appropriate; a customer’s transaction purpose remains important.

sections.heading: Currency treatment does not decide tax or work permission
paragraphs: Thailand appears in the reviewed IRS income-tax index and E-1/E-2 table. Neither supplies a universal withholding rate, transaction permission or individual eligibility. Thai incorporation does not decide the worker’s treaty nationality; assess an actual American assignment separately.

practicalOutput: Establish the receipt category and both actual clock-start dates, then have the bank assess the proposed overseas use.
limitations: The Thai official summary and relevant bank-guideline passages were read with AI assistance. Linked January 2026 Gazette PDFs were blocked to direct retrieval and their reader text was not reliably legible; they are not represented as fully interpreted. Actual category, dates, exclusions and bank documents remain to be applied.
learningSummary: For a covered foreign receipt, the BOT summary distinguishes bringing money back from later selling or depositing it with a Thai bank. Its stated trigger is at least USD 10 million or equivalent. Eligible overseas expenses have a conditional alternative, not general permission to net any payment.
seoTitle: Thai foreign receipts: USD 10 million threshold and unresolved timing

title: Which Timor-Leste offices matter if you ship demonstration equipment?
description: Identify the goods route if equipment will leave Dili; remote teaching and U.S. rental need different decisions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Use the named offices for their stated jobs
paragraphs: The official trade portal describes goods-export steps involving business registration, tax identification, commercial authorisation, customs and product-specific checks. It identifies SERVE for business registration, ATTL for tax identification and MCI for the stated commercial-export authorisation, with relevant commodity authorities and the electronic single window also involved.

Which steps apply depends on the exporter and goods. The portal is an overview, not a complete licence inventory or guaranteed timetable. TradeInvest offers export promotion and information support; ask it about suitable assistance and the current process. Its contact does not verify a U.S. customer, operator or importer.

sections.heading: Compare shipping with renting suitable equipment
paragraphs: In the fictional Dili training-company example, most teaching can be remote but the plan includes demonstration equipment. Identify the exact items, specifications, exporter and U.S. importer, then compare shipping with renting American equipment for the first test.

Rental could avoid that planned shipment, but suitability still needs a technical decision. It does not establish customer demand, local use permission or who can teach on site. Brand/material rights and continuing support also remain separate from the goods process.

sections.heading: Do not assume a regional arrangement supplies U.S. permission
paragraphs: Southeast Asian geography or a regional trade arrangement does not establish a U.S. import preference, operating permission or immigration eligibility. Timor-Leste is absent from the reviewed State Department E-treaty table; a proposed worker’s nationality and other routes need assessment. The founder can remain at home while the proposal is prepared.

practicalOutput: Decide whether demonstration equipment must be shipped, then ask the named offices about that exporter and those goods.
limitations: Actual home-country product steps and U.S. import/use requirements remain to be checked. This resource note does not settle service, banking/tax, sector or work permissions.
learningSummary: Teaching an American operator remotely is different from shipping it equipment. Decide what must actually move before using the Timor-Leste goods-export process.

title: When could the signed U.S.–Vietnam tax agreement affect a payment?
description: The agreement specifies entry and payment-effect conditions, but the current operative status remains unconfirmed here.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: First establish entry into force, then the payment date
paragraphs: The Treasury agreement dated 7 July 2015 requires ratification or approval under both countries’ applicable procedures and written diplomatic notifications when those procedures are complete. Article 29 says the agreement enters into force on the date of the later notification. Finding the signed document does not establish that this happened.

For withholding, the agreement would apply to amounts paid or credited on or after 1 January of the year immediately following the year of entry into force. For other taxes, the stated start is Vietnamese taxable years and U.S. taxable periods beginning on or after that following 1 January. Article 27 information-exchange and administrative-assistance provisions instead take effect from entry into force, regardless of the taxable year or period concerned. Do not use the signature date as a universal start date.

sections.heading: The dated status evidence does not settle today’s treatment
paragraphs: A Vietnamese Ministry of Finance draft report dated 17 July 2025 expressly described the U.S. agreement among those not yet effective. That is positive evidence of the draft’s stated position at that date, not proof that no later change occurred. Vietnam is also absent from the reviewed IRS income-tax treaty index, but list absence alone is not a definitive current status determination.

Current operative status remains unconfirmed here. Withholding is tax deducted before you receive a payment. Keep the full fee, possible deduction and expected receipt separate until current authority and the actual payment and recipient establish the treatment. Neither the signed agreement nor this dated report supplies an automatic royalty rate.

sections.heading: Keep the equipment question separate from the tax assumption
paragraphs: In the fictional maintenance example, the American operator also needs a specialised Vietnamese test device with no identified American replacement or service provider. Even an established payment treatment would not make that device deliverable or serviceable.

Vietnam Customs’ commercial-export guide addresses prohibited products, specialised inspection or licensing, declarations and temporary-export situations. Identify whether the actual item is sold, moved temporarily or replaced locally before costing the shipment. No equipment category is verified here; the U.S. importer’s duties and ongoing serviceability also need assessment. Software rights and remote support are not decided by the goods procedure.

practicalOutput: Establish current operative treaty authority and the actual payment treatment before budgeting a reduced deduction; assess any equipment movement separately.
limitations: Definitive current treaty status, the payment and recipient, product-specific export/import treatment and any U.S. site work remain unresolved. The 2025 draft report is dated descriptive evidence, not current operative law. This is not a complete Vietnamese tax, banking or operating review.
learningSummary: The signed agreement does not make a reduced withholding rate available by itself. Article 29 separates entry into force from the date its withholding provisions would apply; this review has not established that those conditions have occurred.
seoTitle: U.S.–Vietnam tax agreement: entry conditions and withholding timing

title: What does D/USA 101 establish for a German engineer’s U.S. assignment?
description: The certificate concerns social-security coverage; the proposed work and its tax, payroll and credential requirements need their own assessment.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Use the certificate for the coverage question
paragraphs: The Social Security Administration’s Germany page identifies D/USA 101 and the German employer’s request route for the stated social-security coverage exemption. Check whether the actual assignment qualifies and obtain the determination and certificate where applicable.

The certificate is not a visa or an exemption from every American employer tax or obligation. Describe the duties, location and duration so work authorisation, payroll, income tax and any sector credentials can be assessed separately.

sections.heading: Match the response promise to available people
paragraphs: In the fictional maintenance example, a U.S. operator requests four-hour support across several states, but one German head engineer handles complex faults. A certificate would not solve that capacity problem.

Remote diagnosis needs workable coverage hours and limits. A local U.S. specialist needs the capability and any required credentials. A visiting German engineer needs the assignment-specific legal and cost assessment before you rely on the visit. Choose a support promise those facts can sustain; none of these options is declared authorised here.

sections.heading: Use the right treaty for the question
paragraphs: Germany appears in the reviewed income-tax and E-treaty tables. Those listings do not establish a particular tax benefit or immigration eligibility. Ownership, tax residence and the person’s role remain relevant to their respective assessments; a staff-transfer route also requires its own qualifying facts. The founder can remain in Germany if the delivery plan permits.

practicalOutput: Describe the actual engineer’s assignment and check its work permission alongside any applicable coverage-certificate request.
limitations: No assignment, visa, social-security exemption or credential is approved. U.S. employer obligations and other home-country/U.S. operating requirements remain separate.
learningSummary: A German engineer’s technical skill does not make that person immediately available at an American customer site. D/USA 101 addresses a social-security question, not permission to perform the work.
seoTitle: German engineer in America: D/USA 101 versus work permission

title: Can the closed ICEX Next 2026 call fund your launch budget?

The extract covers Spanish applicants, their own internationally marketable offer and brand, services delivered abroad and a staff member responsible for the international project, among other conditions. Its turnover tests and exceptions are programme rules, not American legal revenue categories or permission to sell franchises.

sections.heading: Count the funding you can actually use
paragraphs: In the fictional facilities-training example, finance has treated a hoped-for programme payment as available launch cash. An application, possible reimbursement or positive customer conversation does not fill the gap.
An actual award still has payment conditions. Check those before counting its proceeds, and keep customer payment dates separate from signed contracts.

paragraphs: Spain appears in the reviewed E-treaty table, which has a territorial-scope footnote, and separately in the IRS income-tax index. Neither decides ownership, a person’s nationality or role, an investment case or the applicable withholding rate.

practicalOutput: Recalculate the launch with documented accessible funds and the actual payment conditions of any awarded support.
limitations: The official extract was read with AI-assisted translation, not the complete funding bases. The call remains a closed, dated record; no next opening, eligibility or award is represented. Spanish tax/FX/IP and U.S. requirements need separate review.

sections.heading: Choose the request before choosing the contact
paragraphs: The foreign ministry distinguishes diplomatic market orientation and institutional support from ICE’s specific customer/partner research and market studies. Recognised chambers abroad are private associations. These are not interchangeable operator-certifying bodies.

Ask who buys your service, how the customer procures it or which contacts fit the proposed role.
